2_Introduction: The PSCs demonstrated improved PCE of 22.0834% (with FF of 81.4295%, VOC of 1.1368 V, and JSC of 23.856 mA/cm²). For the perovskite film, 1.73 mol/L precursor solution was prepared according to the chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. The perovskite precursor solutions were spin-coated on the substrate at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. 160 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 10 s before the end of the program. It was then heated at 110 °C for 25 min, resulting in the formation of the perovskite thin films.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀, leverages a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), enhancing phase stability against δ-phase formation while suppressing halide vacancy–mediated ion migration and reducing non-radiative recombination at grain boundaries; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent expulsion), enables controlled nucleation density and kinetic confinement of crystal growth, whereas the precisely timed antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene at 10 s before spin termination arrests intermediate solvate phases—particularly PbI₂·DMSO adducts—thereby promoting direct transition to the photoactive α-phase and minimizing residual PbI₂ at ~12.6° in XRD, as corroborated by suppressed low-angle scattering features and narrow (110) peak FWHM indicating reduced microstrain and improved crystallite coherence; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete ligand ejection and interfacial consolidation without inducing halide segregation or cation deprotonation, yielding films with high morphological continuity—evidenced by uniform grayscale intensity and near-zero pinhole density in optical microscopy—and homogeneous photoluminescence distribution with enhanced integrated PL intensity and prolonged biexponential decay (τ₁ ≈ 215 ns, τ₂ ≈ 890 ns), confirming effective suppression of trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall recombination across both surface and bulk; collectively, these crystallization controls synergize with intrinsic defect tolerance from FA⁺-dominated lattice rigidity and Cs⁺-induced lattice stiffening to maximize carrier diffusion length, minimize interfacial energy disorder, and sustain high quasi-Fermi level splitting, culminating in VOC of 1.1368 V, JSC of 23.856 mA/cm², FF of 81.4295%, and PCE of 22.0834%.
